extraction.name: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
extraction.description: In the quest for artificial general intelligence, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have emerged as a focal point in recent advancements. However, the predominant focus remains on developing their capabilities in static image understanding. The potential of MLLMs to process sequential visual data is still insufficiently explored, highlighting the lack of a comprehensive, high-quality assessment of their performance. In this paper, we introduce Video-MME, the first-ever full-spectrum, Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of MLLMs in Video analysis. Our work distinguishes from existing benchmarks through four key features: 1) Diversity in video types, spanning 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields to ensure broad scenario generalizability; 2) Duration in temporal dimension, encompassing both short-, medium-, and long-term videos, ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour, for robust contextual dynamics; 3) Breadth in data modalities, integrating multi-modal inputs besides video frames, including subtitles and audios, to unveil the all-round capabilities of MLLMs; 4) Quality in annotations, utilizing rigorous manual labeling by expert annotators to facilitate precise and reliable model assessment. With Video-MME, we extensively evaluate various state-of-the-art MLLMs, and reveal that Gemini 1.5 Pro is the best-performing commercial model, significantly outperforming the open-source models with an average accuracy of 75%, compared to 71.9% for GPT-4o. The results also demonstrate that Video-MME is a universal benchmark that applies to both image and video MLLMs. Further analysis indicates that subtitle and audio information could significantly enhance video understanding. Besides, a decline in MLLM performance is observed as video duration increases for all models. Our dataset along with these findings underscores the need for further improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction of the Video-MME dataset involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. To ensure comprehensive coverage across diverse video types, a domain hierarchy was established for sourcing raw videos from YouTube, identifying 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. Videos with varying duration lengths (short: <2 minutes, medium: 4-15 minutes, long: 30-60 minutes) were collected for each category. Corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios were also obtained. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios, representing a range of domains with a relatively balanced distribution of video durations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Out of 900 videos, 156 videos are missing subtitles, as 744 videos are accompanied by subtitles.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Following video collection, high-quality multiple-choice question-answer (QA) pairs were annotated. Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed an entire video and then iteratively created three relevant questions, each with four candidate options, resulting in a total of 2,700 QA pairs. These questions encompass 12 distinct task types, including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis, and are designed to be closely tied to the video content, preventing accurate answers without direct video reference.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A rigorous manual quality review process was conducted. Each QA pair was examined by a different annotator to verify clarity, precision of language, logical consistency of candidate options, and appropriateness of the correct answer. To ensure questions were sufficiently challenging and required video content as a critical clue, text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro, and QA pairs answerable solely based on textual questions were filtered out. Questions not meeting this criterion were returned for revision. Statistical analysis showed Gemini 1.5 Pro achieved less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, confirming the robustness of the video content-based requirement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset and its findings underscore the need for further improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development. The benchmarking, evaluation findings, detailed analysis, and outlined insights are expected to inspire future progress toward more capable and robust MLLMs.
